description: SEQ1 / SEQ2 / SEQ4 / SEQ8 - the row's 0-based ordinal, wrapped to the function's width. Every expectation is a cell measured on a real account. The number belongs to the ROW rather than to the call, so SEQ4()+SEQ4() gives 0,2,4,6 and two different widths report the same row; the count is POST-filter, numbering the rows the projection is handed, while a SEQ inside a predicate counts the rows the filter reads. A FROM-less SELECT is row zero. The width rule is a rule, not a single measurement: SEQ1 spans 0..127 unsigned and wraps, or -128..127 signed, and SEQ2 does the same two bytes wide. Each width declares its own digits - NUMBER(3,0), (5,0), (10,0), (19,0) - and the sign does not widen it. The sign argument must be 0 or 1, but anything whose numeric value lands there is taken, including a string. Converted 1:1 from functions/SeqFunctionTest (now retired); its @BeforeEach fixture is inlined per test. The two declared-type tests read the engine's column metadata in Java, which the live harness cannot carry, so they were skipped live; the suite reads the same fact through a CTAS and INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS instead, and they now run on every backend.

steps.sql: SELECT COUNT_IF(a <> b) FROM (SELECT SEQ4() AS a, SEQ8() AS b FROM nums)
SELECT SEQ4() FROM nums WHERE x > 4
SELECT SEQ4() FROM nums WHERE MOD(x,2) = 0
SELECT x FROM nums WHERE SEQ4() < 2
SELECT MIN(s), MAX(s), COUNT(DISTINCT s) FROM (SELECT SEQ1() s FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT=>1000)))
SELECT MIN(s), MAX(s), COUNT(DISTINCT s) FROM (SELECT SEQ1(1) s FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT=>1000)))
SELECT MIN(s), MAX(s), COUNT(DISTINCT s) FROM (SELECT SEQ2() s FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT=>70000)))
SELECT MIN(s), MAX(s), COUNT(DISTINCT s) FROM (SELECT SEQ2(1) s FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT=>70000)))
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE seq_probe AS SELECT c FROM (SELECT SEQ1() AS c FROM nums)
SELECT NUMERIC_PRECISION, NUMERIC_SCALE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_NAME = 'SEQ_PROBE'
